notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.finding: Flagged as a residency_law companion instrument in an earlier pass; a dedicated research pass this session confirmed it is NOT a standalone legal instrument. Muqeem (منصة مقيم) is an IT service platform built by ELM Company in partnership with the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) for commercial establishments (the establishment-facing counterpart to the individual-facing Absher platform), offering 20+ e-services including iqama and exit-re-entry visa issuance/renewal -- a service catalog, not a legal text with numbered articles. laws.boe.gov.sa does not index any dedicated 'exit-re-entry visa law/regulation'; site-restricted searches surfaced only unrelated instruments (the Diplomatic/Special Passports Law, the Hajj/Umrah entry-visa regulation, the Temporary/Seasonal Business Visa Regulation). The substantive legal basis for exit-re-entry visas already lives inside the already-ingested residency_law track's own Article 14 (معدلة, amended by Royal Decree M/24, 19/6/1397H), which directly governs exit-visa duration/renewal. The associated fee schedule traces to periodic omnibus Council of Ministers fee-adjustment resolutions bundling exit-re-entry visa fees with unrelated service fees, not a subject-dedicated instrument with its own decree number and article numbering. No separate track was built, since doing so would fabricate legal structure (decree metadata, article numbering) that does not exist -- a confirmed negative finding, not an oversight.

notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.law_name_en: "Communications, Space and Information Technology Law" (alleged successor to telecommunications_law)
notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.resolution_status: CONFIRMED NOT A GAP / FALSE LEAD (session follow-up, dedicated verification pass)
notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.finding: The fresh coverage-gap-map scan this session flagged a currency risk: that a newer "Communications, Space and Information Technology Law" (Council of Ministers Resolution 592, 1/11/1443H) might supersede this corpus's already-ingested telecommunications_law track (Royal Decree M/106, itself approved via that same Resolution 592, 1/11/1443H). A dedicated re-verification pass found this was a name-conflation false positive: laws.boe.gov.sa has no law titled "نظام الاتصالات والفضاء وتقنية المعلومات" -- only (1) نظام الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات (M/106, Resolution 592, 1/11/1443H), the law already ingested here; (2) تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية, the REGULATOR's own organizational bylaw (agency governance, not telecom-sector substantive law), a separate instrument this corpus does not track; and (3) the old 2001 نظام الاتصالات (M/12), already known superseded. The flagged finding conflated the already-ingested law's own title with the regulator's 2022 rename from CITC (هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات) to CST (هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية), via a SEPARATE instrument (Council of Ministers Resolution 253, 1444H, Umm Al-Qura Gazette issue 4956) that renamed the regulator and added space-sector oversight -- confirmed via qanoonsa.com, saudipedia.com, ar.wikipedia.org, and multiple Saudi news outlets (amwalplus.com, argaam.com, okaz.com.sa, ajel.sa). CST's own official site (cst.gov.sa) still titles and hosts نظام الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات (Resolution 592, 1443H) as the current, in-force governing law, confirming telecommunications_law's own citation remains correct and current. No rebuild or staleness flag needed.

Substantively: this corpus's own trademark_law track (Royal Decree M/51, 26/7/1435H, as amended by M/49, 26/6/1442H) defines its own Implementing Regulation in Article 1 as the text issued by the GCC Trade Cooperation Committee (لجنة التعاون التجاري) -- approved 21 May 2015, published jointly with the amended base law in the Saudi Official Gazette issue 4625 (1 July 2016), reportedly effective ~27-29 September 2016 (90 days after Gazette publication). This supersedes the OLD, now-irrelevant Ministerial Resolution No. 1723 of 1423H (2002), which was tied to the already-superseded prior national Trademark Law (Royal Decree M/21, 2002) -- the gap-map's own PRIOR estimated_decree pointed at this wrong, outdated instrument and has now been corrected. HOWEVER: the specific Saudi Council of Ministers Resolution / Ministerial Decision number + Hijri date that gave the GCC text domestic force in Saudi Arabia specifically (the Saudi analog of Bahrain's Ministerial Decree 65/2016 or Kuwait's Ministerial Decision 500/2015) could NOT be corroborated by more than one independent source. One candidate number surfaced via an AI-search-synthesis result ('Council of Ministers Resolution No. 66 of 1437H, 6/4/1437H') but is explicitly flagged UNRELIABLE -- it could not be independently corroborated, and other AI-synthesis output in this same research pass demonstrably conflated Bahrain's instrument number with Saudi Arabia's, so this candidate must NOT be used as a citation without primary-source confirmation. WIPO Lex's own record for this Implementing Regulation (ID 19765) is filed under the GCC jurisdiction entity, not Saudi Arabia specifically, and resolves on closer inspection to BAHRAIN's own Ministerial Decision 65/2016 citation -- WIPO Lex has no Saudi-specific record for this instrument. laws.boe.gov.sa was unreachable throughout this research pass (503/connection-reset on every attempt, both WebFetch and direct curl), consistent with this corpus's prior documented experience; no dedicated BOE lawId page for the Implementing Regulation itself surfaced via search-engine indexing either. misa.gov.sa's own hosted PDF (re-uploaded August 2025) still republishes the SUPERSEDED 2002 law text with an internal 'Last Update: May 18, 2022' notation -- a confirmed stale-government-source finding, extending this corpus's own prior documentation of the same conflict.

Recommended next steps before building: (a) attempt a direct primary-source fetch of the SAIP external portal PDF repository (externalportal-backend-production.saip.gov.sa), which proved reachable when BOE and mc.gov.sa did not, specifically for the Implementing Regulation text (only the base law PDF was located this pass); (b) retry laws.boe.gov.sa on a future pass, since its unreachability appears to be a recurring but transient infrastructure issue rather than a permanent block; (c) if a primary Saudi text is obtained, extract its own preamble, which should state its issuing instrument number/date directly.

gaps.estimated_decree: Not issued as a Royal Decree as of this pass. A draft was published by the Ministry of Commerce for public consultation on the 'Istitlaa' platform around March 2022; Commerce Minister Al-Qasabi stated in September 2024 it was 'in its final stages' (still not enacted then). RE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-20 via a dedicated re-check: the official Istitlaa/e-participation consultation listing still carries the 'مشروع' (draft/project) qualifier in its title, not dropped as it would be upon promulgation; Shura Council coverage (Al-Bilad, 22 Apr 2026) shows only incremental recommendations layered on the EXISTING framework, not passage of the comprehensive law; MC's quarterly consumer-protection newsletters through Q2 2026 continue to describe enforcement under anti_fraud_law/e-commerce law only. Two adjacent, narrower, ALREADY-ENACTED laws should not be confused with this one: the Product Safety Law (Royal Decree M/36, 2024, in force since 16 Nov 2024) and the Standards and Quality Law (same batch) -- both confirmed present on laws.boe.gov.sa and distinct in scope. The old, narrow Consumer Protection Society Regulation (Cabinet Resolution 120/1436) appears to have since been cancelled/repealed per an Umm Al-Qura search hit, but that too is not the comprehensive law. Residual gap: direct fetch of mc.gov.sa's own PDF newsletters returned HTTP 503 in both the original and re-check passes; only search-result snippets were available, not full-text verification.
gaps.priority_rationale: Carried forward from the prior version of this gap map, where it was the sole entry not yet resolved by ingestion. If/when enacted, this would likely be a high-priority track (designed to consolidate and modernize consumer-rights protections beyond the existing Anti-Commercial Fraud Law, already covered as anti_fraud_law). Because enactment still cannot be confirmed as of 2026-07-20, building it now risks building a draft/superseded text. Nearly two years have now passed since the Minister's 'final stages' statement (Sept 2024) with still no decree, suggesting this is genuinely slow-moving rather than imminent. Recommend periodically re-checking laws.boe.gov.sa and the Ministry of Commerce's Istitlaa consultation portal for enactment; next-check trigger: the Istitlaa listing drops 'مشروع' from its title, OR a Royal Decree titled نظام حماية المستهلك appears on laws.boe.gov.sa, OR Umm Al-Qura publishes such a decree.
